% {\footnotesize\raggedright
% Prefill (Pre) and decode (Dec) in seconds, oracle pages at medium resolution, prompt
% mode \texttt{none}. \textbf{Rows are grouped by the machine that measured them and the two
% blocks must not be compared}: the H100 prefills the same input roughly fifty times
% faster, so the near-white prefill of the lower block is a property of the machine and
% not of the configuration. The \texttt{machine} field on every row reads \texttt{local}
% and cannot distinguish them; the cache snapshot and the magnitudes are the only handles.
% \textbf{Each row is its own pool}, unlike the matched intersection the paper's cost table
% uses: coverage varies too much across the roster to intersect without one thin row
% shrinking it for every other, so each configuration prints its own per-rung cell count
% and a difference down the table is a difference in pool as well as in configuration.
% Rows whose run tag has a pre-recovery \texttt{results.v100.jsonl} snapshot read it,
% because the live file for those tags has the OOM cells re-run on an H100 and rewritten
% as \texttt{ok}; rows with no such snapshot never went through that pass and read the
% live file. Within the V100 block the card allocation is not uniform either: the larger
% models need 32\,GB cards where the 8B and below fit two 16\,GB ones, so a row prices the
% hardware that could hold it rather than one fixed machine.
% InternVL3-8B and MiniCPM-V generate through one blocking call and record no prefill/decode split, which is reported as \texttt{--} rather than as zero.
% Prefill is the input-bound cost set by the representation and decode the output-bound
% cost set by the prompt and the decode budget; their sum is not end-to-end latency, which
% also carries scheduling and detokenisation, and latency is wall clock rather than an
% absolute. Because \texttt{none} carries no instruction, the model runs to its decode cap
% and every decode figure is an uninstructed upper bound; the Thinking row additionally
% emits reasoning, so its decode is not comparable even within its own block, and its
% \textbf{T}/\textbf{TL}/\textbf{V} cells come from a run that is still in flight.
% Input tokens depend only on the rung, since every Qwen3-VL spec shares a tokenizer, and
% are counts rather than seconds, so they are left unshaded; they cover the 840 of 847
% answerable questions that were fed pages, excluding seven questions on one document
% whose page set resolves empty in every run. Because the V100 rows exclude the cells that
% OOMed, their inputs are lighter than the token rows suggest, so those latencies price a
% lighter input.\par}
